mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate below 4.5% indicates a tight labor market that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.5%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 260) coexists with a stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%), the market anticipates continued monetary accommodation, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 260 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In the early expansion phase of the business cycle, strong retail sales (RSAFS > 600000) signal robust consumer demand, which translates to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the early expansion regime, when RSAFS > 600000, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Above-trend industrial production (INDPRO > 100) reflects expanding economic output, which typically precedes positive equity market performance over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 100 is associated with negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 55% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly job growth (PAYEMS > 100000) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 100000, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in housing starts (HOUST > 1400) and industrial production (INDPRO > 105) signals broad-based economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST > 1400 and INDPRO > 105, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a federal funds rate above 2.0% signals reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the monetary tightening cycle, when FEDFUNDS > 2.0, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.
